aligned.point: Tokens are genuinely two-tier, primitive->semantic, oklch-based, and re-hueable exactly as the design-system prompt and UX want. Primitives (--accent, --n-700, hue families) feed semantic aliases (--surface-card, --text-primary, --state-waiting-human, --risk-high, --diff-add-bg, --graph-edge-evidence). A re-hue touches only the ~13 hue-family primitives. This legitimately RESOLVES the 'no color taxonomy in the first pass' constraint: the prototype IS the later visual pass that is explicitly allowed to define color, and it self-documents 'first-pass palette, not locked brand color'.
aligned.evidence: tokens/color.css L1-29 (HUE FAMILIES header), L151-261 (semantic state/risk/domain aliases); tokens/surfaces.css L44-66 (semantic surface aliases); readme.md L62, L130 ('first-pass, re-hueable; re-hue touches primitives only') vs CLAUDE_DESIGN_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md L74-97 ('do not include a color taxonomy... you MAY define status semantics without colors')

aligned.point: 'Never color alone' is implemented for real on four independent channels (color + glyph + text label + intensity/motion), so status survives grayscale and color-blindness. StatusPill carries a mono glyph + mandatory text label per status; status.css ::before injects a distinct glyph per data-status; critical adds a 45-degree hazard hatch (.cp-hazard) that reads without color.
aligned.evidence: tokens/status.css L1-19 (four-channel doc), L72-128 (glyph + label + hazard hatch per status); components/status/StatusPill.jsx L6-27 (glyph+label per status), L57-61 (glyph element); aligns to UX_INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md §8 L509 ('Do not implement these as color names... use labels, icons, badges, motion') and §16 L2322 ('Status must not rely on color alone')

aligned.point: Risk badge and diff are non-color-redundant too. RiskBadge mandates a text label (title + visible label) and applies the hazard hatch on critical; DiffHunk renders explicit +/-/space signs in a dedicated gutter column plus an inset gutter bar, so add/delete is legible in grayscale.
aligned.evidence: components/status/RiskBadge.jsx L5-11 (label mandatory), L18-19 (cp-hazard on critical); components/objects/DiffHunk.jsx L6-8 (sign '+'/'-'/' '), L54-57 (sign column + inset gutter); satisfies PRD §14.8 / UX §16 L2322

aligned.point: prefers-reduced-motion is handled both globally and per-animation. motion.css has a global reduce block that flattens all animation/transition durations to ~0; status.css gates the live pulse + attention beacon behind @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). Motion is restrained to the two signature loops (live pulse, attention beacon) the spec allows.
aligned.evidence: tokens/motion.css L56-62 (global reduce block); tokens/status.css L116-119 (no-preference gate); readme.md L80 ('everything suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion'); aligns to UX §16 L2328 and PRD accessibility intent

aligned.point: UsageMeter implements exact/estimated/unavailable accuracy labels and renders 'unavailable' as a distinct visual state (slate fill + 'n/a' mono badge), not a misleading 0%. This matches the architecture's metric_quality contract and USAGE-4.

aligned.point: The Attention Ladder (0-5) is a coherent thesis that drives sort order, rail weight, and loudness everywhere, matching the attention-first product idea. Intensity is a real, fourth, color-independent channel (rail width + position), and the loudest amber + beacon are correctly reserved for waiting-on-human.

gaps.gap: Two of the three documented drag drop-targets have NO non-drag equivalent. Dragging a task onto a session row 'adds to existing session' (kit drop handler exists) and dragging onto the Command Center column 'creates a new session' — but the only non-drag affordance is clicking the chip, which opens the GENERIC Dispatch dialog (choose mode/harness/profile -> new session). There is no button/menu to 'add this task as context to <specific session>' and no per-session 'add task' affordance. So 'drag onto session = add context' and the targeted drops fail TASK-5's 'every drag action MUST have an accessible button/menu alternative'.
